minutes.headline: Water commissioners unanimously resolved not to pursue extending the main to Howard Street to serve a subdivision outside the district.
minutes.summary: The board reorganized, reappointed staff and approved minutes, discussed letting landscape and pool companies fill trucks from district water, and spent most of the meeting on Kevin O'Brien's request about a water main to Howard Street. After counsel's advice and public comment against it, the board voted unanimously to drop the effort to supply the outside subdivision. A short exchange followed on a sign needing ZBA approval and on the withdrawal permit.

public_comment.topic: Ms. Bertram said the enabling act would need a district vote to change, voters have twice opposed it, and a cost-benefit analysis would be needed.
Mr. Rogers called the proposal a way to circumvent the district's wishes and urged the board to decide.
A resident worried about precedent, future residents' water protection, and the lack of any successful example.
A resident asked about water sales to trucks for pools and landscaping exceeding the withdrawal permit and the status of the permit increase.

what_happened.line: The Water District board voted unanimously to drop the effort to extend a main from Beal Street to 318 Howard Street to supply a property outside the district.
The vote followed counsel's suggested wording and public comment against the extension, including that voters have twice opposed changing the enabling act.
The board reorganized, approving a chairman 2-1 and reappointing district employees and counsel.
Commissioners were open to selling water to landscape and pool companies if staff devise a slip-based meter-reading system with camera backup and no paid system.
A resident asked about truck water sales exceeding the withdrawal permit and the status of the permit increase; no resolution was recorded.

why_it_matters: The vote leaves the district's service area as it is, and commissioners raised the long-run costs of pump station electricity and tank painting as reasons an outside extension would cost the district.
Water sales to trucks, the withdrawal permit and drought restrictions bear on district revenue, which a commissioner said comes from water sales, so those questions can affect water rates.
watch_next: Whether staff bring back a slip-based meter-reading system for water sales to landscape and pool companies.
The status of the increase to the district's withdrawal permit, raised in public comment without an answer.
